segments.arabic: [1132] حدثنا حفص بن عمر حدثنا شعبة قال: أخبرني عبد الملك عن قزعة قال:
segments.english: Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. Shu‘bah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Malik informed me, from Qaza‘ah, who said:

segments.arabic: سمعت أبا سعيد رضى الله تعالى عنه أربعا قال: سمعت من النبي ﷺ وكان غزا مع النبي ﷺ ثنتي عشرة غزوة
segments.english: I heard Abu Sa‘id, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, relate four things. He said: “I heard from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” He had gone on twelve expeditions with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

segments.arabic: ح حدثنا علي حدثنا سفيان عن الزهري عن سعيد عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ قال
segments.english: Another route: ‘Ali related to us. Sufyan related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa‘id, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: لا تشد الرحال إلا إلى ثلاثة مساجد المسجد الحرام ومسجد الرسول ﷺ ومسجد الأقصى
segments.english: Journeys are not to be undertaken except to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, the Mosque of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and al-Aqsa Mosque.

checkedBody: I heard Abu Said saying four words. He said, "I heard the Prophet (saying the following narrative)." He had participated in twelve holy battles with the Prophet.

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet said, "Do not set out on a journey except for three Mosques i.e. Al-Masjid-AI-Haram, the Mosque of Allah's Apostle , and the Mosque of Al-Aqsa, (Mosque of Jerusalem)."
comparisons.note: Holy battles and the parenthetical following-narrative phrase are supplied in the first introduction. Preserve the selected expedition wording, unfinished introduction and explicit route switch without these additions.

notes: The selected paragraph contains the complete Abu Said introductory fragment followed by an explicit route switch and the Abu Hurayrah three-mosques report. Modern 1188/1189 divide these already-present passages. The web comparison misplaces the second passage under 1133; retain both Arabic routes and the fragment.

The first account remains an introduction only; its four statements are not inserted here from 1139. Both complete routes, the explicit ha route switch, twelve expeditions and all four Prophet honorifics remain. Only the duplicated selected qala is corrected through the explicit two-print evidence record. The travel idiom is rendered as undertaking journeys without an added legal purpose or interpretation.

segments.arabic: [1133] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن زيد بن رباح وعبيد الله بن أبي عبد الله الأغر عن أبي عبد الله الأغر عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه أن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Zayd ibn Rabah and ‘Ubaydullah ibn Abi ‘Abdullah al-Agharr, from Abu ‘Abdullah al-Agharr, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: صلاة في مسجدي هذا خير من ألف صلاة فيما سواه إلا المسجد الحرام
segments.english: A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except the Sacred Mosque.

comparisons.note: The displayed 1133 range begins with the three-mosques statement belonging to selected Arabic 1132, then gives the thousand-prayers report of selected 1133. Do not import the preceding statement or shift identities.

notes: The complete paired Zayd ibn Rabah and Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Abd Allah al-Agharr route leads to the thousand-prayers statement. Its web comparison is the second report under displayed 1133, after misplaced material belonging to 1132.

The paired Zayd ibn Rabah/Ubayd Allah route, repeated Abu Abd Allah al-Agharr name, selected Prophet designation, demonstrative this and thousand-prayers comparison remain. Elsewhere renders fima siwahu without adding an additional mosque noun. The web comparison begins with material from the preceding Arabic entry; it is not copied into this report.

segments.arabic: [1134] حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم حدثنا ابن علية أخبرنا أيوب عن نافع
segments.english: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. Ibn ‘Ulayyah related to us. Ayyub informed us, from Nafi‘:

segments.arabic: ان ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما كان لا يصلي من الضحى إلا في يومين يوم يقدم بمكة فإنه كان يقدمها ضحى فيطوف بالبيت ثم يصلي ركعتين خلف المقام ويوم يأتي مسجد قباء فإنه كان يأتيه كل سبت فإذا دخل المسجد كره أن يخرج منه حتى يصلي فيه قال: وكان يحدث أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يزوره راكبا وماشيا
segments.english: Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, did not pray Duha except on two days: the day he arrived in Mecca, for he used to arrive there in the forenoon, circumambulate the House and then pray two rak‘ahs behind the Maqam; and the day he came to the Quba Mosque. He used to come to it every Saturday. When he entered the mosque, he disliked leaving it until he had prayed in it. He said: He used to relate that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would visit it riding and on foot.

segments.arabic: قال: وكان يقول إنما أصنع كما رأيت أصحابي يصنعون ولا أمنع أحدا أن يصلي في أي ساعة شاء من ليل أو نهار غير أن لا تتحروا طلوع الشمس ولا غروبها
segments.english: He said: He used to say, “I only do as I saw my companions doing. I do not prevent anyone from praying at whatever hour he wishes of the night or day, except that you should not deliberately seek out sunrise or sunset.”

checkedBody: Ibn 'Umar never offered the Duha prayer except on two occasions:
(1) Whenever he reached Mecca; and he always used to reach Mecca in the forenoon. He would perform Tawaf round the Ka'ba and then offer two Rakat at the rear of Maqam Ibrahim.

(2) Whenever he visited Quba, for he used to visit it every Saturday. When he entered the Mosque, he disliked to leave it without offering a prayer. Ibn 'Umar narrated that Allah's Apostle used to visit the Mosque of Quba (sometime) walking and (sometime) riding. And he (i.e. Ibn 'Umar) used to say, "I do only what my companions used to do and I don't forbid anybody to pray at any time during the day or night except that one should not intend to pray at sunrise or sunset."
comparisons.note: Kaaba and Ibrahim are supplied as identifications for the selected House and Maqam wording. Do not insert these identifiers into the selected report.

notes: Both the full Quba/arrival account and the final statement about companions and prayer times are present. Modern 1191/1192 divide this selected paragraph. Retain every timing clause and do not replace the Maqam with an explanatory identification.

The two days, Mecca arrival in the forenoon, House, two units behind the Maqam, Saturday visits, reluctance to leave without prayer, riding/walking report and complete final companions/prayer-time statement remain. The source moves from anyone/he wishes to second-person plural do not deliberately seek; that shift stays visible. No Ibrahim identification or legal commentary is inserted.

segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Muslim related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يأتي مسجد قباء كل سبت ماشيا وراكبا كان عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنه يفعله
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to come to the Quba Mosque every Saturday, on foot and riding. ‘Abdullah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, used to do it.

notes: Keep the Saturday frequency, both walking/riding modes and the final Abd Allah practice clause. The historical closing identification and conjunction differ.

The full named chain, every-Saturday frequency, walking-before-riding order and final Abd Allah practice clause remain, with both companion honorifics. The historical Ibn Umar expansion and printed initial conjunction are not imported into the selected closing wording.

segments.arabic: [1136] حدثنا مسدد حدثنا يحيى عن عبيد الله قال: حدثني نافع عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah. He said: Nafi‘ related to me, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يأتي قباء راكبا وماشيا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to come to Quba riding and on foot.

segments.arabic: زاد بن نمير حدثنا عبيد الله عن نافع فيصلي فيه ركعتين
segments.english: Ibn Numayr added: ‘Ubaydullah related to us, from Nafi‘: “And he would pray two rak‘ahs in it.”

comparisons.note: The explicit Ibn Numayr/Ubayd Allah/Nafi closing route is abbreviated to Nafi added. The complete route must remain in a new translation.

checkedBody: The Prophet used to go to the Mosque of Quba (sometimes) walking and sometimes riding. Added Nafi (in another narration), "He then would offer two Rakat (in the Mosque of Quba)."
comparisons.note: The explicit Ibn Numayr/Ubayd Allah/Nafi closing route is abbreviated to Added Nafi, with a parenthetical another narration.

notes: Retain the complete Ibn Numayr/Ubayd Allah/Nafi appended route and its two-unit addition. The printed chapter heading differs in mosque wording and order; it remains separate from narration.

segments.arabic: [1137] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف أخبرنا مالك عن عبد الله بن أبي بكر عن عباد بن تميم عن عبد الله بن زيد المازني رضى الله تعالى عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:

segments.arabic: ما بين بيتي ومنبري روضة من رياض الجنة
segments.english: Between my house and my pulpit is one of the gardens of Paradise.

notes: The selected report and modern print read my house while the historical print reads my grave. The chapter heading uses grave in all three witnesses. Keep the report and heading distinct and preserve the selected wording; this is not a ruling on variant authenticity.

The selected house wording remains distinct from the grave wording of the historical report and the separate chapter heading. The garden statement is rendered without a metaphorical, legal or eschatological gloss. The complete chain and its Messenger honorific remain.

segments.arabic: ما بين بيتي ومنبري روضة من رياض الجنة ومنبري على حوضي
segments.english: Between my house and my pulpit is one of the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is upon my basin.

comparisons.note: The bracketed explanation locating the grave follows the translated report but is not part of the selected Arabic. Keep it outside the hadith wording.

checkedBody: The Prophet said, "Between my house and my pulpit there is a garden of the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is on my fountain tank (i.e. Al-Kauthar)."

segments.arabic: [1139] حدثنا أبو الوليد حدثنا شعبة عن عبد الملك سمعت قزعة مولى زياد قال:
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Abd al-Malik: I heard Qaza‘ah, the mawla of Ziyad, who said:

segments.arabic: سمعت أبا سعيد الخدري رضى الله تعالى عنه يحدث بأربع عن النبي ﷺ فأعجبنني وآنقنني قال
segments.english: I heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, relate four things from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which pleased and delighted me. He said:

segments.arabic: لا تسافر المرأة يومين إلا معها زوجها أو ذو محرم ولا صوم في يومين الفطر والأضحى ولا صلاة بعد صلاتين بعد الصبح حتى تطلع الشمس وبعد العصر حتى تغرب ولا تشد الرحال إلا إلى ثلاثة مساجد مسجد الحرام ومسجد الأقصى ومسجدي
segments.english: A woman is not to travel for two days unless her husband or a mahram is with her. And there is no fasting on two days: al-Fitr and al-Adha. And there is no prayer after two prayers: after the morning prayer until the sun rises, and after ‘Asr until it sets. And journeys are not to be undertaken except to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, al-Aqsa Mosque and my mosque.

notes: Keep the complete four-part statement, both prayer-time endpoints and all three mosque names. The closing sunset wording differs in the historical print. No legal interpretation is supplied by this intake.

Both hearing statements, the narrator reaction, all four clauses, both prayer-time endpoints, selected two days, and all three mosques remain. Mawla and mahram are retained as source terms without narrowing them to freed slave or adding a legal definition. The afternoon endpoint retains the selected pronoun without importing the historical repeated sun noun. No legal interpretation is supplied.
The historical sunset clause uses taghiba al-shams; selected and modern retain taghrub without repeating the sun noun.
